subject: Escalation: chat completion disconnects causing client retry floods - Healthlytics production (P2)
messages:
From: Gabe Rios <gabe.rios@healthlytics.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:03 -0800
Subject: Production: chat completions disconnecting / clients retrying

Neha —

We're seeing a serious issue in production starting ~08:45 PST. Our clients report that streaming chat completions are being cut off mid-response and client SDKs are retrying aggressively. On our side we see a correlated spike in 429s and 5xx responses, and our telemetry shows a retry storm from many active users.

Impact: several active conversations dropped, elevated error rate (~8% 5xx across chat endpoints) and latency spikes for non-streaming endpoints as well. This is affecting ~12% of active sessions and is causing a surge in support tickets from clinicians.

Attached are the logs and a small trace bundle. We tried switching clients to non-streaming fallback but the retry load is still high. Can you confirm whether this looks like a client-side timeout behavior or an upstream problem? We need immediate guidance and an ETA for mitigation.

Attachments: logs_Healthlytics_20261116.tar.gz (1.4MB), stream_traces_healthlytics_20261116.log (320KB)

Thanks,
Gabe
Gabe Rios
SRE Lead, Healthlytics
gabe.rios@healthlytics.com
(415) 555-0192
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Gabe Rios <gabe.rios@healthlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:23:18 -0800
Subject: Re: Production: chat completions disconnecting / clients retrying

Gabe — thank you for the quick heads-up and the logs. I'm escalating immediately.

Immediate actions from our side (in-flight):
- I've paged Eng on-call (Marissa) and Platform (Jonas).
- CS (Evelyn) is standing by to coordinate customer comms and fallbacks.
- Can you confirm whether your client SDKs are enforcing a client-side idle timeout (we've seen a few vendors default to 30s)? If so, what value?

Quick mitigation I recommend you try now (if not already done):
1) Hard-fail to the non-streaming completion API for a short window to prevent stream-level connection holding.
2) Configure a client backoff with jitter on retries (even a short 500ms base with exponential) to flatten the retry curve.

I'll loop in leadership in 30m if we don't have a mitigation path. Please keep the logs coming; we received the attachments.

-neha
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:48:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Production: chat completions disconnecting / clients retrying

Logging in from Eng on-call. Preliminary triage below.

Summary of what we're seeing (prelim):
- Upstream LB metrics show a sudden increase in connections in ESTABLISHED state from Healthlytics IP ranges around 08:40 PST. Many of these are long-lived streaming connections holding server-side resources (KV cache + per-connection allocs).
- Autoscaler did not immediately add capacity because goroutines for active streams remained open — the autoscaler uses active-requests heuristics that miss long-idle-but-open streams.
- After a short delay the proxy returned 502/504 on new chunks while backend workers were saturated, which triggered client retries. The retry storm amplified the problem and caused 429 throttles on the shared ingress route.

Immediate engineering mitigations (proposed, low-risk order):
A) Apply a temporary idle-stream timeout reduction (from 120s -> 30s) at the proxy layer for the Healthlytics route to free connections quicker.
B) Move Healthlytics to a dedicated route (lower concurrency limits) to avoid affecting shared tenants. Needs ops signoff for capacity shift.
C) Enable ingress-level soft-rate-limiter for newly accepted connections (quick config change).

We attached an excerpt of the traces (see logs_Healthlytics_20261116.tar.gz). Key log snippet below: 

[2026-11-16T08:42:11Z] conn=0x7f3a client=52.24.11.9 stream=open idle=67s worker=busy
[2026-11-16T08:43:09Z] proxy->backend: queue_len=102 worker_busy=98
[2026-11-16T08:43:12Z] backend=timeout -> 502 chunk_write_failed

Next steps I'm taking now:
- I'll open JIRA RI-4621 and attach the full trace and timeline.
- If Neha approves, I'll push the idle-timeout change as a hotfix and enable a per-route soft-rate limit.

Potential customer-visible mitigation timeline: if approved, we can push the proxy timeout + rate-limiter in ~15-25 minutes; moving to a dedicated route will take ~90 minutes with ops coordination.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Software Engineer (On-call), Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:10:22 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Production: chat completions disconnecting / clients retrying

Stephanie — forwarding an escalation from Healthlytics (P2). TL;DR: streaming chat connections are holding worker capacity, autoscaler lag + retry storm caused 502/429 blowups. Eng (Marissa) recommends a fast hotfix (reduce idle-stream timeout + ingress soft-rate-limit) and short-term capacity burst / dedicated route to isolate.

Requesting executive sign-off for two things so we can execute immediately:
1) Approve a 48-hour emergency capacity burst on Dedicated pool for Healthlytics (estimate incremental cost: $6,000/day).
2) Approve a one-off credit if the issue is judged customer-impacting to support retention (we can finalize amount after postmortem).

I'll start the hotfix for the timeout once approved. We also need a clear customer comms note; Evelyn is prepared to send.

Thanks,
Neha
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:29:41 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: chat completions disconnecting / clients retrying

Neha / team — approved.

- Approve 48h capacity burst for Healthlytics; finance and SRE ops, please implement immediately.
- Evelyn: draft a short customer note apologizing for interruption, outline the immediate mitigation taken (timeout + rate-limiter applied), and provide expected timeline for full isolation (up to 90 minutes).
- Legal/Finance: prepare standby for a retention credit; final number after postmortem.

Keep me posted on status + rough timeline for handoff to postmortem. If this looks like a systemic autoscaler/workload-handling gap, let's schedule a leadership review.

—Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Gabe Rios <gabe.rios@healthlytics.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: support@healthlytics.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 13:45:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Production: chat completions disconnecting / clients retrying

Neha / all — thanks for the fast response and for applying the timeout and rate-limit. We've implemented a client-side fallback (non-streaming) and added exponential jitter to retries; initial error rate has dropped and retry amplification looks reduced.

Please proceed with the 48h burst as discussed. We'll watch metrics and share any additional traces. We'll also want the postmortem and the proposed longer-term autoscaler fix.

Appreciate the quick collaboration.

Gabe
